title: Current: charge flow rate
target: Calculate current as charge transferred per time.
criteria: Use I=q/t with seconds and coulombs.
Explain steady charge conservation at a junction.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A wire carries 15 C past one point in 6.0 s. What is average current?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A steady current is 0.40 A. How much charge passes a point in 25 s?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: In the external wire of a simple DC circuit, what direction is conventional current?
options: Always in the direction electrons drift in a metal.
From the switch toward both terminals regardless of polarity.
From the positive terminal toward the negative terminal.
cpa.guide: Conventional current follows positive-charge motion; electrons in metal drift oppositely.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: An arrow follows electron drift in a metal wire. How should a conventional-current arrow be drawn?
options: At right angles to the wire.
No arrow is possible because electrons carry no charge.
In the same direction by definition.
cpa.guide: Negative charge motion corresponds to conventional current in the opposite direction.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: At a junction, 1.8 A enters and one outgoing branch carries 0.65 A. With no charge buildup, what leaves in the other branch?
cpa.guide: Incoming current equals outgoing sum: 1.8 − 0.65 = 1.15 A.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A student says a resistor consumes current, so less current returns to the battery in a steady series circuit. Which correction is accurate?
options: The return current must be zero.
Charge is conserved; the same steady current passes through each series part while energy transfers.
The battery creates new electrons to replace those destroyed.
The student is right because current is energy.
cpa.guide: Series current does not disappear in the load. Energy transfer and charge flow are different quantities.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
